findings.reason: the plan builds new read surface on a premise the repository contradicts, so the author must reconcile §3 against the existing signal maps.
findings.text: §3 states the engine path is unusable because it needs "a ChannelBinding from a packaged signal map, none of which exists for JT-60SA yet", but the tree carries three packaged JT-60SA signal maps built from the same EDDB cache: magnetics.json binds PSRC/Ip -> magnetics/ip/data in A (exactly §3's plasma current from PSRC); pf_active.json binds the MMSYS curCS*/curEF* chains -> pf_active/coil/current/data in A (exactly §3's PF coil currents from MMSYS); tf.json binds cur1TFLKAT; and that engine path is already exercised over this cache at tests/data/test_eddb_cache.py:472 — §2 likewise reads pf_active/wall/magnetics with a raw imas.DBEntry without citing the two in-repo readers that already turn those IDSs into machine geometry: read_geometry_table (imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py:113, documented as "the sole machine-description acquisition route") and MachineArtifactGeometryReader (imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py:726, with read_artifact_pf_active/read_artifact_limiter/read_artifact_magnetics) — this is a census of the reuse misses in one pass

findings.reason: the honest change is to extend the existing read route or state the true gap, either of which rewrites §3's justification and may retire read_channel.
findings.text: §3 adds read_channel beside write_channel (eddb.py:208) as a new read layer over the EDDB cache, justified by the claim that ZarrTransformEngine.read takes a ChannelBinding "from a packaged signal map, none of which exists for JT-60SA yet"; since those maps do exist (above) and the engine path load_packaged_signal_map (imas_ambix/data/signal_map.py:631) + ZarrTransformEngine (imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:156) + VirtualZarrView (imas_ambix/data/virtual_zarr.py:89) is already demonstrated over this cache, the section must state the real gap (the signal maps bind data only, with no time base or unit for the flux-loop and commissioning channels) or extend the existing route, rather than asserting the machinery is absent

reuse_search-1.reason: plan v32 §3 draws the PF coil currents and plasma current as served by the packaged jt-60sa pf_active and magnetics signal maps (chain choice and channel_factor); the §2 half is declined: description_reader and the gs readers return the adapter's table, and §2 hands the raw IDSs to imas-ink's own extract_geometry

thin_wrapper-1.reason: plan v32 §3 states the real gap: the engine path the signal maps feed returns values with no time base or unit, and the maps bind no flux loop, so read_channel supplies time base, unit and the unbound channels; the false 'no JT-60SA map' claim is removed

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the two figure scripts are thin orchestrators delegating to imas-ink, and eddb.read_channel hides the zarr data-and-time layout behind one function; no module spreads its complexity across many shallow wrappers over one mechanism.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — store addressing goes through the catalogue that owns it (load_packaged_machine_map, description_store_root_path) and cache addressing through channel_path/channel_time_path; no shared placement or path-resolution mechanism is forked.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §1b retires the --palette-candidates CLI option and the plot_style module, §2/§3 add no CLI option, and §3 names eddb.read_channel as its one added public name with its reason.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched imas-ink and the EDDB path owners but missed the three packaged JT-60SA signal maps under imas_ambix/data/maps/jt-60sa/ that already bind two of the three channel groups §3 draws, and the two in-repo store-to-geometry readers that read the same IDSs §2 reads.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3 adds read_channel beside write_channel as a new read layer over the EDDB cache and justifies it by a claim about missing machinery that the tree contradicts.
